messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232623984_Integrated_chemicalbiochemical_sample_collection_pre-concentration_and_analysis_on_a_digital_microfluidic_lab-on-a-chip_platform
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1117/12.581955

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Colorimetric Detection of Nitroaromatic Explosive Particles (TNT/DNT) via Reaction with KOH

REAGENTS USED:
  - TNT Sample (commercial grade 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene, or pure 2,4-dinitrotoluene, dispensed by pipette onto the electrowetting chip)
  - KOH Reagent (potassium hydroxide solution that reacts with nitroaromatic explosives to form colored complexes)

STEPS:
1. Dispensing: Manually pipette a droplet of TNT (or DNT) sample and a droplet of KOH reagent onto the electrowetting chip.
2. Merging: Merge the two droplets by applying voltages to the appropriate electrodes.
3. Mixing: Electrowetting-enabled mixing -- transport/shuttle the merged droplet across electrodes to enhance mixing flow, forming the colored reaction complex.
4. Detection: At the completion of mixing, measure the absorbance of the colored complex at room temperature using an on-chip LED (with characteristic absorbance peaks reported at 336 nm and 510 nm for TNT-KOH and 407 nm and 657 nm for DNT-KOH complexes).
5. Disposal: Discard the analyzed droplet after the absorbance reading is taken.

INTERPRETATION: Successful colorimetric explosive detection is confirmed by a linear calibration curve of absorbance versus TNT concentration (y = 0.0056x + 0.0145, R^2 = 0.9863) over the 4-20 ug/mL range, yielding a calculated detection limit of approximately 2.6 ug/mL -- competitive with antibody-based surface plasmon resonance competition assays (7.8 ug/mL). Because the TNT and DNT colored complexes produce mutually independent absorbance peaks, TNT can be quantitatively estimated even in the presence of DNT, a combination common in contaminated soil, supporting on-site, automated colorimetric detection of land-mine and munitions-related nitroaromatic contamination without requiring an experienced chemical analyst.

module fluorescence

manifest TNT_Sample
manifest KOH_Reagent

instructions:

// --- dispensing: TNT/DNT sample and KOH reagent droplets ---
tnt = dispense TNT_Sample
koh = dispense KOH_Reagent

// --- electrowetting-enabled mixing: merge and shuttle across electrodes ---
reaction = mix tnt with koh for 5s

// --- colorimetric detection: LED absorbance measurement of colored complex ---
absorbance = detect fluorescence on reaction for 30s

dispose reaction

ir.content:
main:
	tnt1[0] = dispense(TNT_Sample)
	koh1[0] = dispense(KOH_Reagent)
	reaction1[0] = mix(tnt1[0], koh1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	absorbance1[0] = detect(fluorescence, reaction1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(reaction1[0])
	NOP

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Preliminary results have been obtained from detecting commercial grade 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT) and pure 2,4-dinitrotoluene obtained from Sandia National Labs
Droplets of TNT and KOH were dispensed manually by a pipette on the electrowetting chip

operation_evidence.source_quote: Assays were performed on an electrowetting chip in three steps: dispensing, electrowetting-enabled mixing, and colorimetric detection

operation_evidence.bs_operation: reaction = mix tnt with koh for 5s
operation_evidence.source_quote: These two droplets were merged by applying voltages to the appropriate electrodes. The merged droplet was further mixed by transporting the mixture, causing enhanced mixing flow

operation_evidence.bs_operation: absorbance = detect fluorescence on reaction for 30s
operation_evidence.source_quote: At the completion of mixing, the absorbance was measured using an LED. All the reactions were performed at room temperature
The absorbance spectrum of the color products resulting from the assays for TNT and DNT is shown in Fig. 9

numeric_mismatches.field: reaction = mix tnt with koh for 5s
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes merging and mixing the TNT/KOH droplets by transporting/shuttling them across electrodes but does not report an explicit mixing duration for the TNT/DNT assay specifically (unlike the aerosol/glucose assay's stated ~5s at 50V, Section 2.3); 5s is used here by analogy with that reported mixing duration on the same platform, not a literal value from Section 3.2.

numeric_mismatches.field: absorbance = detect fluorescence on reaction for 30s
numeric_mismatches.note: 'fluorescence' stands in for the paper's actual LED-based colorimetric absorbance measurement (peaks at 336/510 nm for TNT-KOH and 407/657 nm for DNT-KOH, Fig. 9); the 30s duration is illustrative since the paper does not specify a detection integration time for this assay.

numeric_mismatches.field: detection-limit calculation and TNT/DNT independent-peak verification (Fig. 8-9)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are post-hoc data-analysis and a separate bench-spectrophotometer validation experiment (mixing TNT/DNT in various ratios at 505 nm) rather than steps of the on-chip dispense/mix/detect assay itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation.
